MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
Dr. [redacted name]
[redacted location] Oncology Associates

CLINICAL INDICATION
Diagnostic testing for breast cancer genetic susceptibility

TEST PERFORMED
BRCA1 and BRCA2 Comprehensive Analysis
- Full gene sequencing of BRCA1 (NM_007294.4) and BRCA2 (NM_000059.4)
- Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) for large deletion/duplication analysis

RESULTS

BRCA1 ANALYSIS
Sequencing: No pathogenic variants detected
MLPA: No deletions or duplications detected

BRCA2 ANALYSIS
Sequencing: No pathogenic variants detected
MLPA: No deletions or duplications detected

INTERPRETATION
No mutations detected in BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes through DNA sequencing or MLPA analysis. This negative result indicates that the patient is unlikely to have a mutation in BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes.

LIMITATIONS
This test has a detection rate of >98% for sequence variants and large deletions/duplications in the coding regions and splice sites of BRCA1 and BRCA2. However, this analysis does not detect:
- Deep intronic variants
- Regulatory region variants
- Variants in genes other than BRCA1 and BRCA2
- Low-level mosaicism

TECHNICAL NOTES
Methodology: Unidirectional DNA sequencing covering entire coding regions of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes including splice sites. Standard MLPA kits used for exons 1A-24 of BRCA1 and exons 1-27 of BRCA2. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing were performed for all coding exons and intron-exon boundaries. MLPA analysis was performed using MRC-Holland SALSA MLPA kits P002 (BRCA1) and P045 (BRCA2) according to manufacturer's protocols.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted name] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
